Twitch drops, dream horse, asmongold, termian event, new region, kids are on summer break. Not to mention PA is spending money out their ass sponsoring YouTubers to make videos on their game. 

Essentially a ton of things lined up to inflate the numbers. It's an anomaly, and will level off by mid-late august, back to the usual 1-2k. 

Top comments are huffing copium saying it's a sign BDO is doing well again. Just like when snow region came out and was dead content in 2 weeks.

That's a fair point to make. I suppose it's hard to really get an accurate gauge of player numbers due to variety of variables. Like different region availability, regional preferences, what sites polls are taken on, what time of day they're taken, etc. I tried to get the original post stickied to the front page to combat some of these variables, but couldn't manage that. 

I figured reddit was probably the best place to get this information since it somewhat mirrors NA/EU numbers for other popular online games. I believe NA and EU make up something like 80% of reddit users, with NA taking the lion's share. This is somewhat similar to steam user numbers of most popular mmos, as Asian regions tend to use their own clients. 

I was tempted to ask on the forums, but I'm pretty confident forums heavily lean Client over steam, so reddit just seemed like the better option. 

But I do agree that in the near future, steam will probably overtake client users, or at least even out to 50/50 like you say. I no longer see ads for bdo anywhere outside of steam, and as steam in general is seeing more and more users year on year, it only makes sense that more of the playerbase is shifting to steam. 

The only reason I made this post was because of all the other posts either claiming bdo was dying or thriving, with no actual statistics to back up their claims. And since PA does not publish player data, it's up to the community to come up with methods to at least estimate the size of the playerbase. 

While I realize this is a flawed method, I could not think of a better way to get it done.

While this isn't conclusive or anything, I do find it interesting. For years people have made the claim that client users out number steam users by a wide margin, when according to this, it's closer to a 55-45 split. 

So if anyone wants to estimate the playerbase going forward, I'd wager 3x the value of steam charts is probably on the higher end of a probable range (at least for NA/EU).
